subject: Dedicated commit options — H100 / A100 / L40S tradeoffs and pricing
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie@pioneer-analytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: CFO <cfo@pioneer-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing and pricing: Dedicated GPU commit options

Hi Evelyn,

We’re finalizing procurement for a dedicated pool to serve several production inference workloads (13B/70B LLMs, ~2k token avg reqs, embedding pipelines). Before we lock down a commit, can you help with:  
- H100 vs A100 vs L40S: practical perf/$ ranges you’ve seen for long-context generation and embedding throughput; memory constraints we should worry about for 70B variants.
- Typical reserved commit packaging you recommend for a 12–24 month contract (slab vs per-GPU buckets, how to handle burst).
- Example throughput guarantees (tokens/sec or requests/sec) you can commit to per-GPU and how that maps to overage pricing.

We have a hard requirement to avoid noisy/noisy neighbor degradation (99th percentile latency matters more than p50). Also curious about options to mix GPU families to save cost while keeping warm-fallbacks to H100.

Can you send a short commercial sketch + any benchmark artifacts? If this looks good we’ll loop in procurement.

Thanks,
Julie

Pioneer Analytics

Hi Julie — thanks for the note and the context. Short answers up front and a proposed next step: 30-minute call to validate traffic shape and preferred commit window (12 vs 24 months). I’ve attached a concise pricing sketch and a small benchmark summary.

Quick summary (high-level):
- H100: best perf/$ for long-context generation and heavy KV-cache use; 80GB variant lets you serve many 70B variants without quantization. Expect roughly 20–40% better tokens/sec on generation vs A100 for long contexts depending on model and sequence length.
- A100 (40/80GB): good middle ground. If you can quantize and your memory needs fit 40GB, A100 can be ~10–20% cheaper overall for steady-state throughput.
- L40S (48GB): lower unit cost, good for embeddings and short-context workloads. For long context generation it’s cost-effective only as a secondary tier (cold/scale-out) rather than primary.

Packaging we recommend for customers with mixed workloads:
1) Pilot slab (3 months): small pool on A100 or L40S to validate traffic.
2) Reserved Core (12 months): commit for the base sustained qps (mix of A100 + L40S).
3) Reserved Prime (24 months): larger commit with an H100-heavy slab for peak and 99th% latency SLOs; keep a smaller A100/L40S band for less-critical workloads to save cost.

Commercials (very top-level ranges):
- 12-month commit: A100 discounts ~18–22%, H100 ~25–30%, L40S ~10–15% off list for committed hours.
- 24-month commit: add ~8–10pp deeper discounts across families.
- Overage: charged at a blended rate calibrated to the committed slab; burst allowances and pre-bought credits are standard.

Questions for call: expected sustained tokens/sec (or qps), percent of traffic that is long-context generation vs embeddings, and whether you need model-version pinning (affects memory sizing).

If that looks useful I’ll pull Marcus in to share kernel-level perf estimates and Karthik to sketch contract mechanics (billing cadence, buyouts, escape clauses).

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Forwarding Julie’s questions with quick engineering notes — feel free to paste these into the commercial sketch.

On Tue, Jun 12, 2028 at 10:03 AM Julie Park <julie@pioneer-analytics.com> wrote:
> Evelyn — this is very helpful, thanks. A few clarifications before the call: ...

Marcus' notes (engineer):
- 99th% latency target ~500ms for ~1.8k tokens -> approximate concurrency targets (rough):
  * H100 (80GB, optimal kernel set): ~6–8 concurrent gen streams per GPU for high-quality decoding (sampling/temperature). That maps to ~600–1k tokens/sec sustained depending on model.
  * A100 (40GB): if quantized and KV cache optimized, ~4–6 concurrent streams; memory pressure on 70B is tight without 80GB variants or QAT.
  * L40S: ~3–4 streams for long-generation; better for short contexts and embeddings in parallel.
- Quantization: INT8/4-bit quantization is available and yields large memory savings but requires model-compatibility testing. A100 (40GB) + INT8 can sometimes host 70B with aggressive quantization and memory tricks, but expect quality tradeoffs. H100 80GB gives the safest headroom for unquantized 70B.
- Mixed-family fallback semantics: routing is policy-driven. Typical setup: primary (H100) route with warm KV cache; if H100 capacity unavailable, route to A100 pool with adaptive sampling limits (shorter max tokens, strict timeouts) + a visible SLA tier (degraded). We mark those requests as "best-effort" and surface metrics. SLA: fallbacks are supported but latency/quality SLOs are scoped to the primary pool; fallbacks do not inherit full 99th% guarantees unless explicitly included in contract.
- Perf/$ examples (rough numbers for Llama-like 13B/70B workloads, normalized):
  * H100: baseline perf = 1.0x; best for long-context, KV-heavy workloads.
  * A100: 0.75–0.9x baseline depending on quantization and memory config.
  * L40S: 0.5–0.7x baseline for long-gen; much better on short-context/embeddings.
- Operational note: we recommend a small A100/L40S band for background batch work (embeddings, reranks) and H100 reserved for latency-sensitive live serving. That generally optimizes perf/$ while keeping headroom for spikes.

Happy to run a quick focused benchmark if you share a small prompt set and a target model.

Marcus Lin
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Julie — below is a concise commercial proposal based on your ask and Marcus’ notes. If you’re comfortable, I’ll produce a formal quote and loop in our legal/procurement teams.

Proposed commercial sketch (high-level, non-binding):
- Commitment bands:
  1) Pilot (3 months): 6 A100 GPUs (or 8 L40S) to validate traffic and latency.
  2) Reserved Core (12 months): 12 GPUs mixed (4 H100 80GB + 6 A100 40GB + 2 L40S) — designed to cover sustained base qps and background batch.
  3) Reserved Prime (24 months): 18 GPUs with H100-heavy mix (10 H100 80GB + 6 A100 + 2 L40S) — covers peak, with H100 fallback headroom.
- Pricing ranges (committed discount ranges; final $/hour depends on exact slab hours and region):
  * H100: 25–33% off list for 12–24 month commits respectively.
  * A100: 18–28% off list.
  * L40S: 10–18% off list.
- Overage & burst: 10% burst cushion included in month-to-month utilization calculation; overage billed at blended committed-equivalent rate with 10–20% premium depending on short notice.
- SLA and fallbacks: 99th% latency SLO guaranteed for requests routed to the H100 primary pool. Fallback to A100/L40S allowed but marked as degraded tier (exempt from full 99th% guarantee unless you purchase an extended SLA add-on).
- Operational controls: model pinning per route, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies included. We recommend a small canary window the first 2 weeks after cutover.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred commit band (Pilot / Core 12m / Prime 24m).
2) If 12/24 months, we’ll return a formal quote with exact per-GPU hourly rates and contract terms.
3) Optional: provide a 1–2 day benchmark run (we’ll align on prompt set) to firm up perf numbers.

Proposed times to discuss next week: Thu 6/15 9–11am PT or Fri 6/16 1–3pm PT. Please let me know which works and I’ll calendar.

Cheers,
